official_name: Return a Permanent to Its Owner's Hand

objects: one public phased-in battlefield permanent with stable physical and logical identity
timing: one-shot return executes during spell or ability resolution
targets: the bounded compiler accepts one artifact, creature, enchantment, land, nonland permanent, permanent, artifact or enchantment, or creature or planeswalker target
resolution-time target legality is revalidated before preparation
choices: represented destination replacement choices remain owned by the canonical zone-change transaction
hidden_information: the object starts in a public zone and enters its owner's hidden hand unless the move is replaced
opposing private hand contents are not exposed
layers: represented effective card types determine target legality before resolution
complete type-changing and dependency closure remains blocked
replacement_effects: destination replacements are prepared and journaled by the canonical zone-change boundary
copy: ordinary object-copy rules do not change physical ownership
control_change: a permanent controlled by another player still moves to its owner's hand
a prepared plan fails stale if owner or controller changes before commit
zone_change: the moved card becomes a new logical object in its owner's hand
a token moves before later ceasing to exist as a state-based action
source_leaves: the resolved instruction does not require its source to remain unless another rule says otherwise

variants: closed spell, trigger, and activated contexts

implementation.component: typed direct-target compiler, strict return semantic handler, canonical return transaction, and replacement-aware zone-transition owner

known_blockers: graveyard-to-hand recursion and graveyard-to-battlefield reanimation are separate zone families
mass, multi-target, optional, modal, conditional, qualified, linked-result, cost, and self-return clauses remain precise residuals
complete type-changing, copy, face-down, and continuous-effect dependency interactions remain blocked
the mechanic contract is broader than the trusted bounded direct-target capability
